name: Bidirectional Dependent Field Pair (Percent ⇄ Amount)
description: Two editable fields where either one recomputes the other, plus a third derived field. Implemented with sequenced mergedataset/mergedatasetarray actions on onFocusOut — no server call. The canonical case is Discount% ⇄ Discount Amount over a Gross Amount base.
sourceRefs: examples/fapo-fapi-full-breakdown.md 3.8 (row level: PURDET_DISCOUNT_PERCENT ⇄ PURDET_DISCOUNT_AMOUNT), 6.1 (header level: PUR_DISCOUNT_PERCENT → PUR_DISCOUNT_AMOUNT, one-directional)

baseField.description: The amount the percentage applies to, e.g. PURDET_GROSS_AMOUNT.

trailingFormula.description: Action-list splice to run afterwards, e.g. "[fapoEvent1]" or "[calcformula]".

rules: THE TWO MERGES MUST BE SEPARATE ACTIONS. The second reads the field the first writes; expressions inside a single `data` object all evaluate against pre-merge state, so combining them silently uses stale values. This is the single most common way to get wrong totals in this engine.
Operators chain left-to-right with NO precedence: A(*)B(/)raw.100 means (A*B)/100. To group differently, split into more sequenced actions.

onFocusOut (not whenchange) at row level — whenchange would recompute on every keystroke and, where a server proc is involved, issue a request per character. The header-level percent in 6.1 does use whenchange because its maths is purely local.
No divide-by-zero guard exists in the source when the base field is 0. Add one deliberately if you need it.
Always end with the trailing formula splice so header totals follow row edits.
